newsitem.title: HUNGARY: HUNGARY CRITICISES SLOVAKIA'S NEW IMPORT SURCHARGE.
newsitem.headline: HUNGARY CRITICISES SLOVAKIA'S NEW IMPORT SURCHARGE.

text.p: Hungarian Industry Minister Szabolcs Fazakas criticised Slovakia on Wednesday for introducing a seven percent import surcharge this week.

"The Slovak measure contradicts the spirit of CEFTA (Central European Free Trade Agreement)," Fazakas told the daily newspaper Nepszabadsag, adding he hoped the matter could be dissolved before the CEFTA's September summit.
Slovakia, facing serious foreign trade problems, imposed a 7.0 percent import surcharge on all goods except raw materials, effective July 21.

Fazakas said the seven percent surcharge affected 80 percent of Hungary's imports into the neighbouring country, while the earlier Slovak import deposits took away two percent from the price of 40 to 50 percent of Hungary's exports.
Slovakia canceled its first import surcharge, imposed in 1994, in January this year after fierce criticism from the European Union and the World Trade Organisation (WTO).
Fazakas said the WTO would examine if the reintroduction of the surcharge was justified.
"Perhaps the European Union -- with which Slovakia has a trade deficit -- will accept Slovakia's arguments, but we will have to find a bilateral way out of this situtation," he added.
According to the ministry's earlier figures, Hungary's exports to Slovakia in the first five months of this year totalled $108 million, while imports from Slovakia amounted to $152 million.
